title: Right-fibration pullback preserves categorical equivalences
statement: Use quasicategories, right fibrations, categorical equivalences and degreewise pullbacks in the conventions of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], [def-coef-infinity-fibrations] and [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. Let $C$ be a quasicategory and let $q:E\to C$ be a right fibration. Let $A,B$ be small simplicial sets, let $b:B\to C$ be a simplicial map, and let $u:A\to B$ be a categorical equivalence, with $A$ mapped to $C$ by $bu$. Then the induced map $A\times_C E\to B\times_C E$ is a categorical equivalence. No quasicategory hypothesis is imposed on $A$, $B$, or either pullback.

source.place: Corollary 5.6.7.6, dual right-fibration form used in Proposition 7.3.1.14 (02YL). Online source is not archived locally.

proof.text: We first prove a limited assertion needed below. For any small $X$ and any map $c:RX\to C$, use the explicit countable horn completion $X=X_0\subseteq X_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq RX$ of [lem-coef-small-inner-horn-completion]. Put $T_r=X_r\times_C E$ and $T_\infty=RX\times_C E$. Pulling each attaching pushout back to $E$ gives a pushout of the coproduct of the maps $\Lambda_i^n\times_{\Delta^n}Z_a\to Z_a$, where $Z_a=\Delta^n\times_C E$ uses the characteristic simplex of that attachment. Indeed in each degree, a set over $C_d$ is the disjoint union of its fibers; colimits over $C_d$ are computed separately in these fibers and pullback replaces each fiber by copies indexed by $E_d$. This also proves $T_\infty=\operatorname{colim}_rT_r$. Each $Z_a\to\Delta^n$ is a right fibration: a horn square projects to one for $q$ and its filler pairs with the prescribed base simplex. By [lem-coef-right-fibration-inner-horn-pullback], every attaching map is a categorical equivalence, and it is monic degreewise. Hence it is a Joyal trivial cofibration by [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. A lifting square for $T_0\to T_\infty$ against any Joyal fibration extends over every coproduct of attachments, then over its pushout, inductively for $r\in\mathbf N$; the compatible maps give a lift on the colimit. The weak factorization system therefore makes $T_0\to T_\infty$ a trivial cofibration, in particular a categorical equivalence.

source.place: Lemma 5.3.6.6 (02RK), the horn-cell closure argument, restricted to the explicit countable completions.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-small-inner-horn-completion] to $A,B$ in a universe containing all the input. Its restriction map for $X=B$ and target $C$ lifts the monomorphism $\varnothing\hookrightarrow\Delta^0$, so $b$ extends to $\widehat b:RB\to C$ with $\widehat b j_B=b$ exactly. Functoriality gives $v=R(u):RA\to RB$ with $vj_A=j_Bu$, so $\widehat b v$ extends $bu$. Both $j_A,j_B$ are categorical equivalences: their horn-cell descriptions lift against any Joyal fibration by extending across the cells, since inner horns are trivial cofibrations; the weak factorization system of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure] identifies these inclusions as trivial cofibrations. The equation $vj_A=j_Bu$, the hypothesis on $u$, and two-out-of-three show that $v$ is a categorical equivalence. The completions $RA,RB$ are quasicategories, so clause (2) of [lem-coef-joyal-quasicategory-characterizations] says $v$ is a functor equivalence.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.6.1, reduction by inner-horn completion; here the existing functorial completion replaces the two relative factorizations.

proof.text: Put $\widehat E=RB\times_{C,\widehat b}E$ and let $\widehat q:\widehat E\to RB$ be the projection. Pulling horn squares to $q$ shows directly from [def-coef-infinity-fibrations] that $\widehat q$ is a right fibration. Its total space is a quasicategory: fill the projected inner horn in $RB$, then lift that simplex using $\widehat q$. To check it is an isofibration, reverse all ordered simplices. The order involution sends a horn with index $i$ in dimension $n$ to the horn with index $n-i$, so $\widehat q^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a left fibration between quasicategories. For an equivalence $e:\widehat q(x)\to d$, its opposite ends at $\widehat q^{\mathrm{op}}(x)$. The prescribed-target clause of [lem-cbc-left-fibration-equivalence-lift] lifts $e^{\mathrm{op}}$ to an equivalence ending at $x$. Taking opposites gives an equivalence starting at $x$ over exactly $e$. Reversing the inverse-triangle witnesses shows that these edges remain equivalences. Thus $\widehat q$ lifts inner horns and equivalences with prescribed source, the isofibration hypothesis needed next.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.6.1, isofibration of the fibration over the completed base; right-fibration specialization, proved by opposite left-fibration lifting.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-pullback-equivalence] with $y=v:RA\to RB$ and $\pi=\widehat q:\widehat E\to RB$. All three objects are small quasicategories, $v$ is a functor equivalence by Step 2, and $\widehat q$ is an isofibration by Step 3. It gives that the actual projection $RA\times_{RB}\widehat E\to\widehat E$ is a functor equivalence. The simplicial bijection $(a,(v(a),e))\mapsto(a,e)$ identifies its source with $RA\times_C E$ and its map with $(a,e)\mapsto(v(a),e)$ into $RB\times_C E$. Clause (2) of [lem-coef-joyal-quasicategory-characterizations] makes this specified map a categorical equivalence.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.6.1, final equivalence between quasicategories, using the independent isofibration pullback theorem.

proof.text: Step 1 applied to $X=A,c=\widehat b v$ and $X=B,c=\widehat b$ makes both vertical maps in the square with top $A\times_C E\to B\times_C E$ and bottom $RA\times_C E\to RB\times_C E$ categorical equivalences. The square commutes strictly: both composites send $(a,e)$ to $(j_Bu(a),e)=(vj_A(a),e)$. The bottom arrow is a categorical equivalence by Step 4. Two-out-of-three in [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure], first for the composite through the left vertical arrow and then for the composite through the right vertical arrow, gives that the original top arrow is a categorical equivalence. Neither its source nor its target was assumed fibrant.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.6.1, two-out-of-three comparison; the exact original pullback map is retained.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 5.3.6.1 and Lemma 5.3.6.6 (02RK), right-fibration specialization. Online sources read; not archived in literature/. The reduction is written using the existing explicit functorial horn completion and independent isofibration pullback theorem.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q25-5a4bc0924 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, the new node, the full statements of all 7 cited nodes plus the isofibration definition, the citer, the unit, and Kerodon 029H and 02RK online (no local archive exists; WANTED is correct). Item: statement unchanged; it is the opposite of 029H restricted to right fibrations with C a quasicategory and arbitrary A,B, and it is exactly what inner-anodyne-slice-categorical-equivalence uses. Step 1: pullback along E->C commutes with the attaching pushouts and the countable colimit; Z_a->Delta^n is a right fibration; the new node plus monicity gives Joyal trivial cofibrations, which are closed under the cell operations by the lifting description of the weak factorization system. Step 2: the extension of b uses the completion lemma's lifting against the empty-to-Delta^0 inclusion; v j_A=j_B u, two-out-of-three, then clause (2). Step 3: Ehat is a quasicategory; the orientation of the prescribed-target clause under op is correct and gives lifts with prescribed source, which is the isofibration definition. Step 4: the isofibration pullback theorem applies, and the reassociation RA x_RB Ehat = RA x_C E is correct. Step 5: the square commutes because bhat v j_A=bu; two-out-of-three; elementary. Edge cases checked: empty E or A, non-injective u, non-quasicategory A and B. New node: it is the single-inner-horn case of 02RK (right fibrations are cartesian), tested on Lambda^2_1 with p=id, a vertex over 0 and empty Z; it is strictly smaller than the item and is a statement-only node with real searches. Duplicates: my own BFS confirms that cocartesian-categorical-base-change and cartesian-base-equivalence-invariance both reach the item, so citing them would make a cycle; left-fibration-right-anodyne-base-change only gives left anodyne. No cited node reaches the item. I accept the tool use lem-cbc-left-fibration-equivalence-lift. No changes made.
